\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Product Density}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductDensity
\section{Overview}
Finite Gaussian products have the product of scalar densities and obey coordinatewise affine transformation laws. Coordinate moment formulas and density integration identities apply to these product laws.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Norm bound for a coordinate projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_coordinateProjection_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $I$ be a finite index set and let $i\in I$. The coordinate projection $x\mapsto x_i$
from $\mathbb R^I$ to $\mathbb R$ has operator norm at most $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Density of a finite Gaussian product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianReal_eq_withDensity}
\leanok
\proofsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p058-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}$ be a real vector, and let $v\ge0$ with
$v\ne0$. The product of the Gaussian measures with means $c_i$ and variance $v$ has,
relative to Lebesgue measure on $\bbr^I$, density $z\mapsto\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$,
where $p_v(c_i,z_i)$ is the scalar Gaussian density with mean $c_i$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Density Formula for Product Gaussian Integration]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_pi_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianReal_eq_withDensity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite type, let $E$ be a real normed vector space, let $c:I\to\mathbb R$,
and let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$. For every function $f:\mathbb R^I\to E$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)\,d\Bigl(\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)\Bigr)(z)
=\int_{\mathbb R^I}\Bigl(\prod_{i\in I}q_{c_i,v}(z_i)\Bigr)f(z)\,dz,
\]
where $N(c_i,v)$ is the Gaussian measure with mean $c_i$ and variance parameter $v$, and
$q_{c_i,v}$ is its density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Affine transformation of a Gaussian product measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianAffine_pi}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $s\in\mathbb R$.
The map $y\mapsto(c_i+s y_i)_{i\in I}$ sends the product of standard Gaussian measures
on $\mathbb R^I$ to the product of Gaussian measures with means $c_i$ and variances
$s^2$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_affine_gaussian_pi_eq_density}

\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $s\in\mathbb R$
be nonzero, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I} f(c+sY)\,d\gamma_I(Y)=\int_{\mathbb R^I}\left(\prod_{i\in I}
p_{c_i,s^2}(z_i)\right)f(z)\,dz,
\]
where $\gamma_I$ is the product of standard Gaussian measures, $dz$ is product Lebesgue
measure, and $p_{m,v}$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a centered coordinate square]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge0$, and choose
$i\in I$. Under the product measure whose $j$th coordinate has Gaussian distribution
with mean $c_j$ and variance parameter $v$, the function $z\mapsto(z_i-c_i)^2$ is
integrable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered second coordinate moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianReal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge0$, and
choose $i\in I$. If $Z=(Z_j)_{j\in I}$ has independent Gaussian coordinates with means
$c_j$ and common variance $v$, then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I}(z_i-c_i)^2\,d\Bigl(\bigotimes_{j\in I}N(c_j,v)\Bigr)(z)=v.
\]
\end{lemma}
